01109.origin: Sony Computer Entertainment asked the studio Punchline (makers of Chulip) for a horror game. Punchline chose psychological horror over zombies, ghosts or slashers. Shuji Ishikawa directed, with about 25 developers, and Shirogumi made the CGI cutscenes. It came out in Japan on 19 January 2006.
01109.reached: Sony decided not to release it in the US, saying it did not fit its corporate image. Atlus USA announced at E3 2006 that it would publish it instead. The US release was on 12 September 2006, as a normal retail disc in a limited number of copies.

rarity.note: Wikipedia says the game was published in a limited number of copies, but gives no print run. Sony skipped the US, so Atlus was the only US publisher. The UK, Australia and New Zealand releases were cancelled.

wow.text: Sony passed on the US release. Atlus stepped in and announced its North American edition at E3 2006.

04729.origin: Poop Slinger is a joke casual shooter from Diggidy.net, LLC, in which you fire projectiles at targets across 9 maps and 3 modes. It launched digitally on the PS4 in August 2018. A small outfit called Limited Rare Games then put it on disc.
04729.reached: Sold directly through the Limited Rare Games website, which opened physical sales on 1 April 2019. It was a one-off boutique run and never reached normal retail shelves. 84 orders are reported to have been honoured.

rarity.note: The physical run was sold only through one tiny website and, by press accounts, only 84 copies sold. Accounts differ on how many were planned (820 or 1,000), so the sold figure is the safer evidence.

wow.text: Limited Rare Games reportedly hoped to sell about 1,000 discs but only 84 orders came in, which made this one of the smallest physical PS4 releases ever.
The publisher's name echoes Limited Run Games, and it is described as a one-person operation said to be based in Russia.

04941.origin: Tamashii is a pixel-art puzzle-platformer with horror touches, inspired by obscure Japanese games of the late 80s and 90s. It was made by Vikintor, a Brazilian developer, and published digitally on the PS4 by Digerati.
04941.reached: A physical run by Limited Rare Games was announced on 31 October 2020 and open for pre-order for only a few hours. It was sold through the Limited Rare Games website. The developer said he had not known about it and later said the publisher confirmed it was legitimate.

rarity.note: The disc was available for just a few hours through one small site. The seller claimed more than 90 sold, but buyers reported ordering several copies each, so the real number is unknown. It is reported as sold out.

wow.text: The developer said he had no idea his game was being sold on disc and told fans not to buy until the publisher confirmed it was real.
Pre-orders stayed open for only a few hours on Halloween 2020, and one buyer reportedly ordered five copies.

06919.reached: It never reached normal retail. Limited Run Games planned it as an exclusive bonus for collectors who bought every Limited Run Vita release. The plan was dropped after copies had already been manufactured, and a few copies reached the market anyway.

rarity.note: Never sold at retail. The bonus plan was cancelled after production, and only a few copies are known outside Limited Run. GIGA calls it the rarest PS Vita game of all, but that is one outlet's claim and other sources name other Vita titles.

wow.text: The card was meant as a thank-you for anyone who bought every Limited Run Vita release. The plan was scrapped after copies were made, which angered the community.
GIGA calls it the rarest PS Vita game of all, and the game started life as a digital-only 2018 release.

07019.origin: VVVVVV is Terry Cavanagh's gravity-flipping platformer. It came out on PC in 2010 and on Vita in 2015. Nicalis published the Vita version and made the physical cards.
07019.reached: No regular retail run is confirmed. Nicalis said hole-punched copies were samples given to Sony as a courtesy for its employees. In April 2019 Nicalis announced a physical Vita release, but sources do not confirm it shipped at retail.

rarity.note: The only cartridge copies sources describe are promotional samples, marked by a punched hole in the back, with no confirmed retail run. GIGA says the Vita version is the only physical release of VVVVVV at all.

wow.text: Per GIGA, the Vita card is the only physical version of VVVVVV on any platform. Promo copies often carry a hole punched through the back cover.

09714.origin: Martha Is Dead is a psychological thriller by LKA, a studio in Florence, Italy, published by Wired Productions. It is set in German-occupied Tuscany in the last years of World War II. The PS5 Collector's Edition was a boutique box built around the game, with soundtrack, books and tarot cards.

rarity.note: The publisher states 1,000 units of the PS5 Collector's Edition, and Limited Run Games lists a separate 300-copy run marked sold out and manufacturing complete. Both are small boutique runs, and the edition is no longer in production.

wow.text: Only 1,000 PS5 Collector's Editions were made. Each was individually numbered with a certificate, sold in the UK and Europe through Wired's store, with a North American run through Limited Run Games.
The box holds a triple-vinyl soundtrack, metal case, hardcover art book, The White Lady book, a graphic novel, 22 tarot cards, a coin pack, a poster, a map and a Steam code.
The PlayStation releases were edited: certain graphic scenes lost their interactivity and some references were cut. The game is uncut on other platforms.
